headline: National Park Vehicle Tags and Cades Cove Access
reservation: Great Smoky Mountains National Park requires a valid parking tag for any vehicle stopping for more than 15 minutes; these must be purchased via official portals or local kiosks. Cades Cove vehicle-free days vary by season, typically affecting Wednesday access during summer months. Lodging in the valley requires a separate reservation through the official park concessionaire.

days.title: Valley History and Wildlife

stops.name: Cades Cove Loop Road
stops.detail: An 11-mile one-way loop featuring 19th-century cabins, churches, and frequent bear sightings.

stops.name: Abrams Falls Trail
stops.detail: A 5-mile round-trip hike through pine-oak forest leading to a high-volume waterfall.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes for the loop road; traffic often moves at a crawl.
days.note: Arrive before 8 AM to avoid the heaviest vehicle congestion.

days.title: River Rapids and Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 10 AM from Little River Road

stops.name: Great Smoky Mountains Heritage Center
stops.detail: View relocated historic buildings and learn the traditions of the Appalachian settlers.

stops.name: Little River
stops.detail: Participate in seasonal tubing or fly fishing in the clear, mountain-fed waters.

days.driving: Local transfers under 15 minutes; river flow varies by recent rainfall.
days.note: Check local water levels; tubing may be suspended during low flow.

days.title: Underground Wonders and Ridge Views

stops.name: Tuckaleechee Caverns
stops.detail: Tour a massive underground cave system featuring ancient stalagmites and a 58-degree constant climate.

stops.name: Foothills Parkway
stops.detail: Drive the 'Missing Link' section for elevated panoramas of the highest Smokies peaks.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for parkway overlooks; conditions vary with mountain fog.
days.note: Caverns require stairs and walking over damp, uneven surfaces.

intel.title: Park Entry Requirements
intel.text: Display a valid park parking tag on your dashboard at all trailheads. Compliance is checked regularly by rangers at popular spots like Abrams Falls.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Townsend is the last reliable stop for fuel before entering the Cades Cove area. There are no gas stations within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Mountain Topography
intel.text: Expect total loss of cellular signal once you pass the Townsend park entrance. Download offline maps for Cades Cove and Tremont navigation.

intel.title: Vehicle-Free Access
intel.text: The Cades Cove loop is closed to cars on specific summer Wednesdays for cyclists. Check the official NPS calendar to avoid being turned away at the gate.

intel.title: Secondary Roads
intel.text: Gravel roads like Rich Mountain Road are one-way and subject to seasonal closure. Always verify current road status at the Townsend Visitor Center.

plan.arrival: Collect vehicle at TYS airport and stop in Maryville for groceries before checking into Townsend cabins or riverside campgrounds.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are suitable for the main loop, though high-clearance helps on Tremont gravel spurs.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Foothills Parkway overlooks provides the clearest views of the blue mountain ridges.
